did_you_know.text: The psalm’s title states that it is intended for the music director, designated as a maskil, and attributed to David.
In the context of the psalm, the Ziphites are mentioned as those who told Saul that David was hiding among them.
David asks for deliverance in God’s name and also appeals to Him to judge him by His might.
The psalmist asks God not only to hear his prayer but also to listen to the words of his mouth.
The enemies are described as “strangers” and “ruthless men” who seek his life, and the text adds that they do not set God before them.
Despite the danger, David declares, “Surely God is my helper,” presenting God as the one who sustains his life.
The psalmist asks that evil return upon those who lie in wait for him—that is, upon the enemies who oppose him—and that they be cut off according to God’s truth.
David promises to offer the Lord a freewill sacrifice and to give thanks to His name, because it is good.
At the end of the psalm, the psalmist testifies that God has delivered him from every trouble and that his eyes have seen the defeat of his enemies.
